evidence: RECORDING MODE IS F / LABEL RECORD IS STANDARD / BLOCK CONTAINS 0 RECORDS — classic IBM mainframe FD clauses
ASSIGN TO UT-S-<ddname> — IBM JCL DD-name assignment convention
SD for sort work file (SORTWK01) — IBM DFSORT/SYNCSORT pattern
COPY 'I#CLLPPN' / COPY 'I#CLLPX0' — IBM-style copybook names with # character
EJECT compiler directive used as page-break
Sequence-number area used for change tags (e.g. VH0812 in columns 1-6)
Max line length exactly 72 — fixed-format mainframe standard

purpose.summary: Batch report program (CLLPG637) that reads parameter and sequential input files containing letter-emission data (LADO107 and related files), sorts records via a SORT work file, and generates a client-level report (RELATO) plus an image file (IMAGAVIS). It was later adapted for Brazilian 'Lei da Transparência' compliance.

notable_features: OCCURS 11 TIMES table within sort record for multiple debt/charge occurrences
Multiple COPY statements referencing IBM-style copybooks (I#CLLPPN, I#CLLPX0)
Change-tag prefixes in sequence-number area (VH0812) for audit trail
FILE STATUS fields for all files
S9(13)V99 COMP-3 signed monetary fields (IOF, interest, penalties, legal costs)
verdict.notes: Source is truncated to the first ~16 KB of an 89 KB file (1239 lines total). All visible evidence is consistent with IBM mainframe COBOL production code from a Brazilian financial institution, dated 1998 with modifications through 2014. The # character in copybook names is standard for IBM z/OS PDS member naming. No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS found; purely batch sequential processing.
